root_cause.text: `ima_kexec_post_load()` called `kimage_map_segment()` for kexec segments assuming they always had `IND_SOURCE` pages to `vmap()`, but CMA-backed kexec allocations store the segment directly in CMA and have no source pages, so the mapping logic dereferenced the wrong assumption and triggered the warning in `kimage_map_segment()`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states that “there is no IND_SOURCE for the kexec segment” when allocated in CMA, while “the current implementation of `kimage_map_segment()` assumes that IND_SOURCE pages exist and map them into a contiguous virtual address by vmap()”; the patch fixes this by returning `page_address(image->segment_cma[idx])` early and only calling `vunmap()` when `is_vmalloc_addr(segment_buffer)`, confirming the bug was the incorrect assumption about CMA-backed segments needing `vmap()`-style mapping.

vuln_statements.content: * Collect the source pages and map them in a contiguous VA range.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a fast path in kimage_map_segment() to return the address of CMA-backed segments instead of remapping them.
intent_record.what: In kimage_map_segment(), a new local variable `struct page *cma` was added, the function now reads `image->segment_cma[idx]` into it, and if that pointer is non-NULL it immediately returns `page_address(cma)` before executing the existing segment mapping logic.
intent_record.how: At runtime, segments backed by a CMA page now bypass the normal page collection and virtual mapping path and instead use the direct address of the CMA page. This changes behavior so that CMA-backed segments are handled explicitly and avoids remapping work for those cases.

intent_record.intent_summary: Guard vunmap() so kimage_unmap_segment() only unmaps vmalloc-backed segment buffers.
intent_record.what: The call to vunmap(segment_buffer) was replaced with a conditional that first checks is_vmalloc_addr(segment_buffer) and only calls vunmap() when the pointer is a vmalloc-backed address.
intent_record.how: At runtime, kimage_unmap_segment() now avoids passing non-vmalloc addresses to vunmap(), preventing invalid unmapping operations on segment buffers that were not mapped via vmalloc. This makes the function safe to call with either vmalloc-backed or non-vmalloc pointers.

Adding a fast path to return the CMA-backed address avoids the faulty remapping path and fixes the assumption mismatch.

The fix directly addresses the root cause by handling kexec segments that are not vmalloc-backed. Since CMA-backed segments have no source/vmalloc pages to map or unmap, guarding vunmap() in kimage_unmap_segment() is part of the same incorrect assumption about segment backing storage.
